subject: math
title: Multiplying Two-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Grade 5 Multiplying Two-Digit Numbers Worksheets: Area Model and Standard Algorithm (Free, Ontario)
standard_text: Represent and solve problems involving the multiplication of two-digit whole numbers by two-digit whole numbers using the area model and using algorithms, and make connections between the two methods
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 math worksheets on multiplying two-digit numbers for the Ontario curriculum: multiples of 10, the area model, partial products, the standard algorithm, estimating and word problems. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Split both numbers into tens and ones and multiply every part. The area model and the standard algorithm give the same answer.
key_sub: 23 × 14 = 200 + 30 + 80 + 12 = 322. In the algorithm, row 1 is 23 × 4 = 92 and row 2 is 23 × 10 = 230 (start it with a zero). 20 × 30 = 600, not 60.
body_html:
Multiply by multiples of 10

Use a fact you know. 20 is 2 tens and 30 is 3 tens. 2 × 3 = 6, and tens × tens = hundreds, so 20 × 30 = 6 hundreds = 600. Two zeros, one from each number.

For 23 × 30, find 23 × 3 = 69, then write one 0: 23 × 30 = 690.

The area model

Split each number into tens and ones. Draw a rectangle with one part for each pair. Multiply each part, then add all four parts.

Partial products

Write the same four parts in columns, lined up by place value, and add them.

The standard algorithm

Make one row for each digit of the bottom number. Row 1 multiplies by the ones digit. Row 2 multiplies by the tens digit, so it starts with a placeholder zero (green). Then add the two rows.

How the two methods connect

Each row of the algorithm is one row of the area model. For 23 × 14, row 1 is 23 × 4 = 92 (the 4 row: 80 + 12). Row 2 is 23 × 10 = 230 (the 10 row: 200 + 30). 92 + 230 = 322, the same answer.

Estimate to check

Is 38 × 24 = 912 reasonable?

Round to the nearest ten: 40 × 20 = 800. 912 is close to 800, so it makes sense. An answer like 228 or 9120 is far off.

Answer: Yes

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
20 × 30 = 60Tens × tens = hundreds: 20 × 30 = 600
Forgetting the zero in the tens row (38 × 24 = 152 + 76 = 228)Row 2 is × 20, so write 0 first: 760
Only two parts (23 × 14 = 200 + 12)There are four parts: 200 + 30 + 80 + 12 = 322
Not adding a regrouped digit (38 × 4 = 122)Write it small and add it: 3 × 4 + 3 = 15, so 152
Adding the regrouped digit firstMultiply first, then add: 3 × 4 + 3 = 15, not (3 + 3) × 4

faq.q: What multiplication do Grade 5 students learn in the Ontario math curriculum?
faq.a: Expectation B2.6 asks Grade 5 students to multiply two-digit whole numbers by two-digit whole numbers using the area model and algorithms, and to explain how the two methods connect.

faq.q: How do you teach 2-digit by 2-digit multiplication?
faq.a: Start with the area model: split both numbers into tens and ones and add the four parts, so 23 × 14 = 200 + 30 + 80 + 12 = 322. Then show the standard algorithm, where each row is one row of the area model.

faq.q: Why do you put a zero in the second row?
faq.a: The second row multiplies by the tens digit. In 38 × 24 the 2 means 2 tens, so the row is 38 × 20 = 760, not 38 × 2 = 76. The zero keeps the digits in the right places.
20 × 30 = 600. 2 tens × 3 tens = 6 hundreds. A common mistake is 60, which forgets that tens × tens makes hundreds.

A bakery makes 48 butter tarts each hour. How many butter tarts does it make in 12 hours?
items.e: 12 hours × 48 tarts, so multiply 48 × 12. Row 1: 48 × 2 = 96. Row 2: 48 × 10 = 480 (write the placeholder 0, then 48 × 1 = 48). Add: 96 + 480 = 576.

items.q: Each coach bus seats 56 people. The school books 14 coach buses for a trip to Ottawa. How many people can ride?
items.e: 14 buses × 56 people, so multiply 56 × 14. Row 1: 56 × 4 = 224. Row 2: 56 × 10 = 560 (write the placeholder 0, then 56 × 1 = 56). Add: 224 + 560 = 784.

items.q: A farm stand packs 87 cartons of eggs. Each carton holds 12 eggs. How many eggs is that?
items.e: 87 cartons × 12 eggs, so multiply 87 × 12. Row 1: 87 × 2 = 174. Row 2: 87 × 10 = 870 (write the placeholder 0, then 87 × 1 = 87). Add: 174 + 870 = 1044.

items.q: A community garden is 23 m long and 14 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = 23 m × 14 m, so multiply 23 × 14. Row 1: 23 × 4 = 92. Row 2: 23 × 10 = 230 (write the placeholder 0, then 23 × 1 = 23). Add: 92 + 230 = 322.

items.q: A sugar bush fills 46 boxes with bottles of maple syrup. Each box holds 12 bottles. How many bottles is that?
items.e: 46 boxes × 12 bottles, so multiply 46 × 12. Row 1: 46 × 2 = 92. Row 2: 46 × 10 = 460 (write the placeholder 0, then 46 × 1 = 46). Add: 92 + 460 = 552.

items.q: Winter mitts cost $16 a pair. The school buys 45 pairs for a winter clothing drive. How much does it spend?
items.e: 45 pairs × $16, so multiply 16 × 45. Row 1: 16 × 5 = 80. Row 2: 16 × 40 = 640 (write the placeholder 0, then 16 × 4 = 64). Add: 80 + 640 = 720.

items.q: A field trip to a pioneer village costs $18 for each student. 56 students go. What is the total cost?
items.e: 56 students × $18, so multiply 18 × 56. Row 1: 18 × 6 = 108. Row 2: 18 × 50 = 900 (write the placeholder 0, then 18 × 5 = 90). Add: 108 + 900 = 1008.

items.q: A food drive collects 37 boxes of soup. Each box holds 24 cans. How many cans is that?
items.e: 37 boxes × 24 cans, so multiply 24 × 37. Row 1: 24 × 7 = 168. Row 2: 24 × 30 = 720 (write the placeholder 0, then 24 × 3 = 72). Add: 168 + 720 = 888.

items.q: Kai works out 58 × 34 = 406. Estimate to check. Is his answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 58 × 34 is about 60 × 30 = 1800. 406 is far from 1800, so it cannot be right. Kai forgot the placeholder 0 in the tens row. The correct answer is 1972.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 67 × 48?
items.e: Round each number to the nearest ten. 67 has 7 ones, so it rounds up to 70. 48 has 8 ones, so it rounds up to 50. 70 × 50 = 3500 (tens × tens = hundreds). The exact answer is 3216, close to 3500.

items.q: A classroom floor is covered with square tiles in 32 rows of 28 tiles. How many tiles are there?
items.e: 32 rows × 28 tiles, so multiply 28 × 32. Row 1: 28 × 2 = 56. Row 2: 28 × 30 = 840 (write the placeholder 0, then 28 × 3 = 84). Add: 56 + 840 = 896.

items.q: In the Terry Fox Run, each of the 27 students in Nathan's class raises $35. How much does the class raise?
items.e: 27 students × $35, so multiply 35 × 27. Row 1: 35 × 7 = 245. Row 2: 35 × 20 = 700 (write the placeholder 0, then 35 × 2 = 70). Add: 245 + 700 = 945.

items.q: The hockey arena in Zoe's town has 24 rows of seats. Each row has 38 seats. How many seats are there?
items.e: 24 rows × 38 seats, so multiply 38 × 24. Row 1: 38 × 4 = 152. Row 2: 38 × 20 = 760 (write the placeholder 0, then 38 × 2 = 76). Add: 152 + 760 = 912.

items.q: Liam practises piano for 35 minutes a day. How many minutes does he practise in 28 days?
items.e: 28 days × 35 minutes, so multiply 35 × 28. Row 1: 35 × 8 = 280. Row 2: 35 × 20 = 700 (write the placeholder 0, then 35 × 2 = 70). Add: 280 + 700 = 980.

items.q: Which is the best estimate for 86 × 29?
items.e: Round each number to the nearest ten. 86 has 6 ones, so it rounds up to 90. 29 has 9 ones, so it rounds up to 30. 90 × 30 = 2700 (tens × tens = hundreds). The exact answer is 2494, close to 2700.

items.q: Maya works out 72 × 39 = 2808. Estimate to check. Is her answer reasonable?
items.e: Estimate: 72 × 39 is about 70 × 40 = 2800. 2808 is close to 2800, so the answer is reasonable.

items.q: A skating rink rents skates to 64 people each hour. How many people rent skates in 13 hours?
items.e: 13 hours × 64 people, so multiply 64 × 13. Row 1: 64 × 3 = 192. Row 2: 64 × 10 = 640 (write the placeholder 0, then 64 × 1 = 64). Add: 192 + 640 = 832.

items.q: Hockey tickets cost $42 each. What is the best estimate of the cost of 19 tickets?
items.e: Round 19 to 20 and $42 to $40. 20 × $40 = $800. The exact cost is 19 × $42 = $798, very close. (Rounding $42 up to $50 gives $1000, which is too far off.)
